topStories.headline: Nordstrom Rack Announces Return to Union Square, Signing Lease at 2 Stockton Street for Fall 2027 Opening
topStories.dek: The off-price retailer will occupy 51,500 square feet at the corner of Stockton and Market, filling a storefront vacant since Forever 21 departed in 2019.
topStories.body:
Three years after closing both of its downtown San Francisco locations, Nordstrom Rack is coming back. The Seattle-based retailer announced Wednesday, October 15, that it has signed a lease at 2 Stockton Street — a 51,500-square-foot corner storefront at Market and Stockton in the Union Square neighborhood — with the store scheduled to open in fall 2027.

The building, owned and managed by Invesco Real Estate, has been largely empty since Forever 21 vacated in 2019 and a brief candy-store tenant subsequently closed. According to The Registry, the building is also slated for a $60 million renovation that includes a vertical office addition and replacement of its Market and Stockton street facades.

Nordstrom co-CEO Erik Nordstrom pointed to the city's improved downtown momentum in a company statement: "The city has many wonderful assets, and it has clearly built momentum in making downtown a great place for customers." Mayor Daniel Lurie, who announced the deal on Instagram, framed the return as a shift in business sentiment, saying in a statement: "Three years ago, companies were leaving San Francisco. Today, they want to be here, and Nordstrom Rack's decision to return to the heart of our city is another sign of the growing confidence in San Francisco."

The announcement lands one week after Uniqlo drew large crowds to its newly reopened flagship at 801 Market Street. The SF Standard reported that brokers had predicted Uniqlo's high-profile opening could have a follow-the-leader effect on other retailers weighing a return. Los Angeles Apparel — the brand founded by American Apparel's Dov Charney — separately confirmed in early October that it has signed a lease at 111 Powell Street, Uniqlo's former home. Union Square's retail vacancy rate currently stands at roughly 15 percent, down from a peak near 23 percent but still well above the 6.4 percent recorded before the pandemic.

topStories.headline: 'I Am' Comes Down: Embarcadero's 45-Foot Nude Sculpture Dismantled After 18 Months, Clearing Path for New Park
topStories.dek: Crews disassembled Marco Cochrane's towering steel-mesh figure this week; the platform where it stood will become part of the $40 million Embarcadero Park renovation.
topStories.body:
Dismantling of the towering sculpture known as "I Am" began Monday, October 13, and by Tuesday the head of the 13,000-pound steel-mesh figure had been lowered to the pavement at Embarcadero Plaza. The piece, originally titled "R-Evolution" and recently renamed by its creator Marco Cochrane, had stood across from the Ferry Building since April 2025 — twelve months longer than its originally planned six-month run, after two successive extensions.

Cochrane created the 45-foot artwork for the 2015 Burning Man festival; it was modeled after Bay Area model Deja Solis and was part of San Francisco's Big Art Loop project, a public art initiative featuring sculptures along a 34-mile trail across the city. The work had been originally intended for Union Square, but was placed at Embarcadero Plaza after Union Square Park officials cited engineering complexities. Cochrane's team is trucking the piece to his Petaluma warehouse for refurbishing; according to the SF Chronicle, its future home has not been determined and the work is listed for sale or lease.

The removal marks a milestone for the Embarcadero Park renovation project. The platform where "I Am" stood will be absorbed into the planned five-acre park — to be named Embarcadero Park, with the former plaza section designated Art Agnos Plaza — that is scheduled to break ground by year's end and open in early 2028. That project will replace the existing concrete plaza and adjacent Sue Bierman Park with a central lawn, performance stage, dog play area, outdoor fitness stations, and improved pedestrian connections to the waterfront.

Reactions to the sculpture's departure were divided. KRON4 reported a range of opinions from passersby, from relief to regret. In a statement quoted by the Chronicle, Cochrane reflected on the work's tenure: "'I Am/R-Evolution' has stood in San Francisco as an invitation — to feel your own strength and your own tenderness at the same time."

topStories.headline: Sue Bierman Playground Reopens Today as Embarcadero Park Design Heads to Arts Commission on Monday
topStories.dek: The children's playground closed for tree work since September 28 has been cleared to reopen; the full park redesign goes before the SF Arts Commission's Civic Design Review Committee on October 19.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Recreation and Park Department confirmed in an October 2026 project update that Sue Bierman Playground at Embarcadero Park has now reopened, following a two-and-a-half-week closure that began September 28 to accommodate tree removals around the play area. The department's notice had indicated a target reopening of Friday, October 16.

The tree work is part of the broader Embarcadero Park Renovation Project, which will eventually merge Embarcadero Plaza and Sue Bierman Park into a unified five-acre waterfront park. The next public milestone is Monday, October 19, when the project team will present the proposed park design to the San Francisco Arts Commission's Civic Design Review Committee at 2:00 p.m. The meeting is held in hybrid format — in person at City Hall, Room 416, and online — and is open to the public.

The $40 million renovation is being delivered through a public-private partnership, with approximately $18 million in voter-approved public funding and up to $20 million in private contributions, including a $10 million commitment from Crankstart. The Rec and Park Commission unanimously approved the names "Embarcadero Park" and "Art Agnos Plaza" on September 17, 2026. Construction is currently projected to begin in late 2026, with the completed park expected to open in early 2028.

With the removal of the "I Am" sculpture this week clearing the plaza site, the project continues to advance toward groundbreaking. Planned features include a large central lawn and permanent performance stage, picnic and dining areas, an enclosed dog play area, outdoor fitness stations, stormwater gardens, and improved pedestrian connections to the Ferry Building and the Bay.

moreNews.headline: Los Angeles Apparel Confirms First SF Store at 111 Powell Street, Union Square
moreNews.body: Los Angeles Apparel — the basics clothing brand founded by American Apparel's Dov Charney — confirmed on October 2 that it will open its first San Francisco location at 111 Powell Street in Union Square, the former Uniqlo space. The company, which currently operates stores in Los Angeles and New York, was described by the Colliers broker who handled the deal as drawn to "the energy and the foot traffic" of the district. No opening date has been announced. The move is part of a wave of retailers signing new leases in Union Square as the area's retail vacancy rate falls toward 15 percent.

moreNews.headline: SF Office Market Posts Strongest Annual Absorption Since 2019, South Financial District Leading Recovery
moreNews.body: San Francisco's office market absorbed 5.5 million square feet over the past twelve months — the strongest annual total since 2019 — according to a NAI NorCal market report published October 15, 2026. Vacancy fell to 20.2 percent, a 2.7-point annual decline driven by AI, technology, and life-science leasing. The South Financial District led performance, with Anthropic's January 2026 lease of the full 420,000-square-foot building at 300 Howard Street cited as one of the market's anchor transactions. Asking rents in the Financial District average about $59 per square foot, up 6.8 percent year-over-year.
